each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt

many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

The task requires finding the transformation rule from the demonstration pair. In the demonstration pair (9x18 grid), the output grid is identical to the input grid except that the order of the rows is reversed. Specifically, the first row of the input becomes the last row of the output, the second row of the input becomes the second-to-last row, and so on. The internal content of each row (the sequence of numbers) remains unchanged.

For the new instance, the input is a 1x3 grid (`[[2, 9, 8]]`). Applying the rule of reversing the row order to a single-row grid results in the same grid, as there is only one row to stay at index 0.

-   **Input Row 0**: `[2, 9, 8]`
-   **Output Row 0** (which should be Input Row 8 in a 9-row case, or Input Row 0 in this case): `[2, 9, 8]`

Thus, the output grid should be `[[2, 9, 8]]`.

{"action": "submit", "grid": [[2, 9, 8]]}
